name: @abyssinia-labs/sokie
stderr:
sokie: no command "stdio".

Usage: sokie <command> [--json] [--workspace <slug>]

Commands:
  init       Start a server from an OpenAPI or Swagger spec, or a GraphQL schema.
  check      Check the server in dir the way a deploy would, without deploying.
  tools      List the tools in tools/, or show one, with its effect and findings.
  skills     List the skills in skills/, write a new one, try it, or install a server's.
  call       Call one tool as an agent would, on sokie dev or a deploy.
  test       Run the cases in tests/ on sokie dev or a deploy.
  fmt        Write sokie.json the one way Sokie writes it.
  dev        Run the server locally on the real runtime, reloading on every edit.
  edit       Open a server's files in your editor, with sokie dev running.
  pull       Bring a folder from sokie edit up to date with production.
  login      Sign this computer in to Sokie.
  logout     Sign this computer out of Sokie.
  whoami     Show who this computer is signed in as, and the workspace commands work in.
  workspace  Show, list or choose the workspace commands work in.
  deploy     Deploy the server in dir and wait until it is live.
  deploys    List a server's deploys, compare two, or restore an earlier one.
  link       Deploy the server from its GitHub repository.
  secrets    List, set or remove the linked server's secrets.
  keys       Make, list and revoke API keys for CI, scripts and agents.
  domains    Serve your servers at your own domain: one for the workspace, or one per server.
  requests   Ask an owner or admin for a change that's theirs, or answer what members asked.
  logs       Show the linked server's calls, as far back as your plan keeps them.
  audit      Show who changed what in your workspace over the last year.
  config     Show or shorten how long CLI sign-ins last.
  update     Install the newest sokie, the way this one was installed.

--json              Print one JSON document for a script, instead of lines.
--workspace <slug>  The workspace to work in, for this run (or $SOKIE_WORKSPACE).

sokie <command> --help shows a command's options, and sokie --version the version.
sok is the same command.
